chunks: Be hopeful for relief, and do not lose hope in the Spirit of God, for the best deed in the sight of God, the Exalted, is waiting for relief.
As long as the believing servant endures, rely on God when you pray the two rak'ahs of Fajr, for in them you are granted your desires.

Do not enter the sanctuary with swords, and let none of you pray with a sword in front of him, for the Qibla is safer. Complete your Hajj with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) when you go to the House of God, for leaving it is ingratitude, and you were commanded by that.
And complete [your visits] to the graves which God has made incumbent upon you to honor and visit, and seek sustenance there.
Do not underestimate minor sins, for the small is counted and returns to become major.

Lengthen your prostration, for there is no deed harsher on Satan than to see the son of Adam prostrating, because he was ordered to prostrate but disobeyed, and this one was ordered to prostrate and obeyed and was saved.
Frequently remember death, the day of your exit from the graves, and your standing before God, so that calamities become light for you.
When one of you suffers from his eyes, let him recite the Verse of the Throne and intend in his heart that it is a cure, for he will be healed, if God wills.
Guard against sins, for there is no calamity or lack of sustenance except due to a sin, even a scratch, a stumble, or a misfortune.
God, the Exalted, said: 'And whatever misfortune befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.'
Frequently remember God while eating, and do not be arrogant, for it is a blessing from the blessings of God and sustenance from His sustenance, upon which you must show gratitude and praise.
Be good companions to blessings before they pass, for they will depart and testify against their owner regarding what he did with them.
Whoever is content with God with a little of sustenance, God will be content with him for a little of deed.
Beware of negligence, so that regret does not occur when regret is of no use.
When you encounter your enemy in war, speak less and remember God much, and do not turn your backs on them lest you incur God's wrath and deserve His anger.
And when you see among your brothers in war a wounded man, or one who has been weakened, or one upon whom your enemy has set his sights, strengthen them with yourselves.
Do good deeds as much as you are able, for it protects from bad deaths.
Whoever among you wishes to know his rank with God, let him look at God's rank with him regarding sins; thus will be his rank with God, the Blessed and Exalted.

The best thing a man can keep in his house for his family is a sheep. If he has one sheep, the angels sanctify him once a day. If he has two, they sanctify him twice a day. And so for three, saying: 'Blessed are you.'
When a Muslim becomes weak, let him eat meat and milk, for God has placed strength in them.

When you intend to perform Hajj, prepare for the journey's needs with some of what strengthens you for travel, for God says: 'And if they had intended to go out, they would have prepared for it preparation.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: The two rak'ahs of dawn prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the key spiritual and practical teachings of Imam Ali regarding daily life and worship in this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage from Imam Ali’s (AS) teaching in al-Khisal reflects the Shia emphasis on 'Intizar al-Faraj' (waiting for relief) as an active spiritual state rather than passive waiting, deeply rooted in the concept of divine decree (Tawhid al-Af'al). It integrates practical daily conduct with eschatological awareness, linking minor sins to major calamities and highlighting the spiritual efficacy of specific acts like the two rak'ahs of Fajr and prolonged prostration. The text serves as a comprehensive guide for the believer, balancing inner devotion with outward social and military conduct, grounded in the Quranic principle that afflictions are often consequences of human actions.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 27-4 Be hopeful. Do not lose hopes in God’s Mercy. The best deed in the sight of the Honorable the Exalted God is being hopeful for relief so that one can survive with that hope.
You should seek God’s help by reliance on Him when you say your morning prayers, since that is the time when the rewards are bestowed.
Do not enter a shrine with a sword.You should not put the sword in front of you while you pray, since the Qibla (prayer direction) is a secure turning point.

Whenever you go on the Hajj pilgrimage, you should also go and visit the shrine of God’s Prophet (MGB). It would be ungrateful not to do so.You should also visit other shrines which the Honorable the Exalted God has made it incumbent upon you to visit. You should ask for your share of daily bread there.
Do not underestimate minor sins since they might lead to major sins.

Lengthen your prostration because nothing is harsher for Satan to bear than to see the prostration of man, since Satan was ordered to prostrate but he disobeyed and man was ordered to prostrate and he obeyed and was saved.
You should often remember death and your departure from the grave and standing up in front of God so that difficulties become easy for you.
Whenever you get a pain in the eye you should recite the verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi) hoping that you get better if God wills.
I advise you to abstain from committing sins since any calamities, restrictions in your share of the daily bread, scratches, or bruises are due to committing sins.
The Honorable the Exalted God said, ‘Whatever misfortune happens to you, is because on the things your hands have wrought, and for many (of them) He grants forgiveness.’

You should often remember God when you eat food. You should not rebel since the food is also one of God’s blessings, and it is a part of your daily bread. It is incumbent upon you to thank and praise God for it.
It would be better if you are grateful for the blessings when you get them and before they are gone. Blessings will testify as to how their owner treated them.
God would be pleased with a little bit of good deeds of anyone who is pleased with a little bit of daily bread from God.
I admonish you against immoderation as it will result in regret when there is no use in regret.
When you are in the battlefield and you encounter your enemies, you should talk less and remember God a lot. You should not flee since then you will face God’s Wrath.
When you encounter your wounded brethren you should rescue them.
You should do as many good deeds as you can so as to be saved from a bad death.

If you wish to know about your rank in the sight of God, you should consider God’s rank in your sight when you are committing sins. This would be your rank in the sight of the Blessed the Sublime God.

The best thing you can get in your house for your wife is a sheep. The angels would sanctify you once a day, if you have one sheep in your house. They would sanctify you twice a day if you have two sheep in your house. They would sanctify you three times, if you have three sheep in your house.
Whenever a Muslim gets weak, he should eat meat and dairy products since the Honorable the Exalted God has placed strength in them.

Whenever you decide to go on the Hajj pilgrimage, you should prepare for the trip in advance as the Honorable the Exalted God says, ‘If they had intended to come out, they would certainly have made some preparation.’
